Author: FLYBYME <mangoraft@gmail.com>

    spec: server-side rendering, the decision and why the obvious fix is wrong
    
    Written while single mode was being built and left in a scratchpad. page.ts
    emits an empty <body> on every site, and flatten.ts says in its own header
    that it is the SSR path -- but no server imports it, and mesh-serve does not
    depend on mesh-web at all.
    
    The obvious fix does not work: a release pins a kernel artifact and different
    sites on one edge run different kernel versions, so a cdn with a bundled
    kernel would render every site with the wrong one. That is the failure
    DeclarationSchema.kernel exists to prevent, made invisible because it would
    happen in our HTML rather than someone's browser.
    
    Three options costed. Recommends build-time prerender now -- cheap, safe,
    keeps the cdn a pure byte server, honest that it buys a shell and not content
    -- with live rendering designed but gated behind B6, because the moment a
    third party's part executes on our hardware it stops being about protecting
    the site and starts being about protecting the platform.
